stories.head: SAS AI Navigator launches on Microsoft Marketplace as AI governance SaaS tool
stories.plain: SAS released a dedicated SaaS platform to inventory every AI model a company runs, then align those models to risk and compliance rules. Landing on Microsoft Marketplace makes it immediately purchasable by enterprise IT buyers. As regulators push for AI accountability, a tool that gives compliance teams a complete map of AI in use directly shapes how marketing AI gets approved and governed.

stories.src: Agile Brand · via Agile Brand Guide
stories.head: InMobi: 36% of U.S. storefronts ready for AI agent checkout; DoubleVerify adds ChatGPT Ads attribution
stories.plain: Two findings in one digest: more than a third of U.S. storefronts can now handle purchases made by an AI shopping agent without a human in the loop, and DoubleVerify has wired attribution measurement into ChatGPT ad placements. Both signal that agentic buying and AI-native ad channels are moving from experiment to infrastructure fast.

stories.head: Predactiv People Model: a foundation model built specifically for marketing audiences and behavior prediction
stories.plain: Predactiv detailed a patent-pending AI foundation model trained on marketing and consumer behavior data rather than general text. It promises more accurate audience prediction and behavioral modeling than adapting a generic LLM. A purpose-built foundation model for marketing changes what agencies and data owners can build on top of — and who controls the underlying intelligence.

stories.head: Captello Intelligence Cards deliver live CRM records and AI summaries at the moment of lead capture
stories.plain: Captello's update surfaces a full account record — firmographics, open deals, contacts, tasks, and an AI summary — the instant a badge is scanned or a meeting attendee is checked in. This turns a passive data-collection step into real-time lead qualification, reducing the lag between event contact and sales action and changing how field teams prioritize follow-up.

stories.head: How to turn customer signals into smarter email automation
stories.plain: A practical guide on using behavioral signals — including inaction, not just clicks — to trigger more relevant automated email campaigns. For practitioners building or auditing their engagement stack, it offers a clear framework for signal-driven automation that sits between basic rules-based sends and full AI decisioning, making it useful for teams at any maturity level.

stories.head: Braze expands AI from content creation to campaign operations
stories.plain: Braze is moving its AI beyond writing copy into automated campaign decisioning — checking campaign logic, choosing timing and channel per person, and connecting to external LLMs like Claude. This shifts Braze from a messaging tool into a platform that acts on decisions, which changes how marketers evaluate and buy customer engagement software.

stories.head: Constructor launches Agentic Checkout powered by Stripe inside a single AI agent experience
stories.plain: Constructor and Stripe let shoppers go from AI-driven product discovery all the way to completed purchase without leaving the agent. This is a concrete example of an AI agent controlling a full commercial transaction — not just recommending — which reshapes how retailers think about checkout and conversion infrastructure.

stories.head: SAS AI Navigator launches on Microsoft Marketplace as a SaaS AI governance tool
stories.plain: SAS has released a dedicated SaaS product that lets compliance, risk, and AI teams build a complete inventory of all AI systems and align them with governance policies — now purchasable directly through Microsoft Marketplace. As AI regulations tighten, having an auditable register of automated decisions is becoming a buying requirement, not a nice-to-have.

stories.head: Salesforce acquires AI customer research startup Listen Labs
stories.plain: Salesforce is bringing AI-run customer interviews and simulated customer behavior directly into its CRM and agent layer. Acquiring the capability — rather than building it — signals that synthetic customer insight is becoming a core CRM feature, changing how marketers budget for research and how Salesforce competes with pure-play insight vendors.

stories.head: AI local search usage surges 6X, fragmenting the digital ecosystem
stories.plain: SOCi data shows consumers using AI for local search has grown six-fold, and they now loop across multiple platforms to verify results before acting. This fragmentation of local search intent forces marketers to optimize for AI-generated answers — not just Google rankings — fundamentally changing local SEO and media spend decisions.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI Search Is Fragmenting Discovery — and Rewriting SEO Rules
body: AI-powered local search has surged 6× in usage, pulling queries away from traditional search engines and toward conversational engines that generate their own shortlists. Brands that relied on classic keyword ranking are finding themselves invisible in results they never optimized for.

Practitioners are now being forced to build visual SEO strategies and optimize content specifically for generative engine models — a discipline that barely existed 18 months ago. The decision that changes: your SEO budget and content architecture must now account for multiple AI-mediated discovery surfaces, not just one search index.
ev: MarTech · Visual SEO for AI Search

themes.head: Agentic AI Moves Into the Revenue Stack
body: AI agents are no longer confined to content drafting — they are now closing transactions. Constructor's agentic checkout collapses product discovery and purchase into a single agent session, while Captello's Intelligence Cards turn live event check-ins into real-time lead qualification without human intervention.

Meanwhile, GTM teams are already reporting they have lost track of which agents are running which tasks across their stacks. The governance gap is real: deploying agents faster than you can audit them creates compounding risk for compliance, data quality, and brand consistency.
ev: MarTech · GTM Teams Losing Track of Agents

themes.head: Speed Without Quality: AI Made Marketing Faster, Not Better
body: A recurring editorial thread this month is the uncomfortable truth that AI accelerated output before it improved outcomes. Campaigns publish faster, copy is generated in seconds, and personalization pipelines are automated — but customer expectations have risen in parallel, leaving tolerance for mediocre experiences at an all-time low.

Canva's B2B CMO Meghan Gendelman puts the counter-argument directly: AI investment demands a proportional investment in brand, because undifferentiated fast content erodes brand equity. The practical decision for marketers is to pair every efficiency gain with a deliberate brand-quality checkpoint, not just a speed metric.
ev: MarTech · AI Makes Customers Expect More
Agile Brand · Brand Investment alongside AI

themes.head: AI Governance & Evidence Infrastructure Become Non-Negotiable
body: Across B2B and enterprise contexts, the conversation has shifted from whether to use AI to how to prove it works. SAS launched an AI Navigator specifically to supercharge governance, while Salesforce's acquisition of Listen Labs signals a push to ground AI decisions in richer, auditable customer research rather than model assumptions alone.

The evidence problem is structural: marketing teams can produce AI outputs at scale but cannot yet produce the causal proof that those outputs drove revenue. Until measurement infrastructure catches up, budget decisions will remain contested — making investment in attribution and AI audit tooling as urgent as the AI itself.

themes.head: The Human Skills Gap Reshapes Marketing Careers
body: Job posting analysis shows that AI skill requirements in marketing roles have surged, but the pipeline for developing those skills is broken — early-career positions are being eliminated rather than retrained, creating a cohort gap that will hollow out mid-level talent within two to three years. Apprenticeship models are being proposed as the structural fix.

At the same time, platforms like Braze are expanding AI from content creation into campaign operations, meaning the required skill set now spans prompt engineering, workflow design, and agent oversight — not just copywriting. Marketers who do not invest in this upskilling now will find themselves dependent on vendors for capabilities that should be in-house.
ev: MarTech · What Job Postings Say About AI Skills
MarTech · Braze Expands AI to Campaign Operations

month.takeaway: The month's signal is unified: AI is restructuring every layer of the marketing stack simultaneously — discovery, execution, governance, and talent — faster than most teams have built the evidence, oversight, or skills to manage it safely.
